(Top left) RAM mixed rCF- PP, (Top middle) Carding rolls, (Top right) feeding the rCF-PP to the carding rolls; (Bottom right) conduct the carding slowly to minimize fiber attrition; (Bottom middle) Slowly pull off the mat from the carder on a Teflon carrier film; (Bottom left): Release the Teflon film to obtain the carded mat 64 The carded mats were then stacked in a compression mold and pressed under pressure and temperature of 320F into plates on the Carver press as shown in Figure 87. About 10 layers of the mat were used to produce a 3 to 3.5 mm plate. These plates were used to generate the mechanical test data. Figure 87. Carded mats were stacked in a compression mold and pressed into plates. The plates were cut to ASTM coupons Figure 88 provides the flexural strength and modulus for the mixes from Table 8. The average flexural strength was noted to be ~90 MPa and the flexural modulus to be 7.5 GPa. The fiber lengths in these specimens are < 3mm and this can be the primary reason for the lower modulus. However, the strength of 90 MPa is excellent. Of all the mixes, Mix 4 provided the highest value for flexural strength and modulus. This mix had 50% less rCF which appears to help with the deagglomeration and create a more uniformly carded mat. These tests provided some early indication of the optimal mix conditions for RAM and the carding ability of the mix and resulting mechanical properties.
